newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: SOCCER-AFRICA NATIONS CUP MASCOT SEEKS NAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AFRICA NATIONS CUP MASCOT SEEKS NAME.

text.p: Burkina Faso, organisers of the 1998 African Nations Cup finals, have chosen a mascot for the competition -- but have yet to choose a name.

Souley Mohamed, head of the organising committee, presented the mascot -- a ball with a smiling face, football boots and a traditional Sapone hat -- on Friday, saying it had been chosen from among 300 suggestions.
He said a name would be chosen in two weeks time and invited members of the public to come forward with suggestions.
The Sapone hat -- a sort of Mexican-style straw hat with a pompom on top -- is a symbol of hospitality among Burkina Faso's main ethnic group, the Mossi.
Souley said that the budget for the two-yearly competition -- the 21st of its kind -- was 1.68 billion CFA francs in costs with projected receipts of 1.87 billion CFA francs.
He said that work on the facilities had slipped behind schedule but would be ready for the kick-off on February 7, 1998.
The draw will take place on September 25, 1997. The final is planned for February 28, 1998.
